questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

She cracked the most funniest joke at the party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 4)**

__
 
• The phrase "the most funniest" is** incorrect **because "funniest" is already in the superlative form.
 
• Using both "most" and "funniest" together is** redundant.**
 
• The correct phrase should be "the funniest".

Hence, the correct statement is **'*She cracked the funniest__ joke at the party*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When using adjectives in the superlative form **(e.g., funniest, tallest, smallest), do not use** **"most"** before them.
 
• **Superlative adjectives inherently indicate the highest degree of comparison,** so adding** "most"** is** unnecessary and grammatically incorrect.**

The subway __fare is go__ up next week.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'is go up' is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be **'is going up'** to indicate the** future continuous tense.**
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb 'is going' should be used in place of the incorrect form **'is go'.**

 Hence, the correct statement is **'*The subway fare is going up next __week*.'**

• The **future continuous tense **is used for actions that will be ongoing in the future.
 
• It is formed using the structure: **subject + will be + present participle (verb+ing)**.
 
• **Example: *I will be traveling to New York next month*.**
